messages.subject: Stecked percentage bar chart
parts:
I have a data frame that look like this:

         A   B    C D  E    F
    1 No cog No cog No cog  No cog No cog No cog
    2 No cog No cog No cog  No cog No cog No cog
    3 No cog No cog No cog  No cog No cog No cog
    4 No cog No cog No cog  No cog No cog No cog
    5 No cog No cog No cog  No cog No cog No cog
    6 No cog No cog No cog  No cog No cog No cog

I want to create a stacked bar chart similar to the above image.

I know that I have to use the package reshape2 to change the format of my table.
I did:
    melt(cog, id.vars=0)->m_cog
This gives me the right format
    head(m_cog)
    Warning message:
    attributes are not identical across measure variables; they will be dropped
    > head(m_cog)
      variable  value
    1      A No cog
    2      A No cog
    3      A No cog
    4      A No cog
    5      A No cog
    6      A No cog

However, this gave me also the following warning:

    Warning message:
    attributes are not identical across measure variables; they will be dropped

Now, in the first place, I understand the meaning of the mess but I have no clue how to fix it

Then I try to get the graph with:

    qplot(data=m_cog, geom="bar", x=variable,  fill=factor(value))

But this give me the count of element on the y axis and to the percentage.
I looked over and over on the web, but I really do not understand how to fix this.
what am I missing here?
